name: Unpopular Opinion, Defended
why_it_works: A contrarian opener triggers a small argument in the viewer's head, and people stay to see if you can back it up. Defending it with three plain reasons turns the provocation into earned authority, and the disagreement in the comments spreads the post further.

hook.pattern: Lead with a short opinion most of your industry would argue with, said flatly with no hedging.

variables.name: brand
variables.description: Business, firm, show or artist name

variables.name: contrarian_take
variables.description: The short opinion others would argue with
variables.example: you shouldn't hire the lawyer with the most billboards

variables.name: reason_one
variables.example: billboards measure ad budget, not trial experience

variables.name: reason_two
variables.example: big-volume firms often hand your case to whoever is free

variables.name: reason_three
variables.example: the right question is who will actually work your file

variables.name: discussion_prompt
variables.example: What did you wish you'd asked before hiring?

visual.prompt: Vertical 9:16 portrait of the host or owner of {{brand}} sitting on a stool against a dark plain wall, one hard key light from the side, slight smirk, looking straight into the lens
Vertical 9:16 photo illustrating the first reason for {{industry}}, real-world setting, natural light, documentary style, no text in image
Vertical 9:16 photo of a busy, impersonal office or crowded scene related to {{industry}}, cool light, slightly chaotic, documentary style

beats.voiceover: Three, and this is the real one: {{reason_three}}.

visual.prompt: Vertical 9:16 slow push-in on the host of {{brand}} leaning forward toward camera, same dark wall and side light, serious calm expression

craft.notes: The opinion must be defensible, not edgy for its own sake. Order the reasons so the strongest is last and say so out loud. End on a real question so the disagreement goes into the comments instead of the unfollow button.

do_not: Pick a take you can't defend with facts
Attack a named competitor or person
Hedge the hook with 'maybe' or 'I think'
compliance: Law firms: no guarantees of outcomes, no 'specialist' or 'expert' claims unless certified, and follow your state bar's advertising rules (some require an 'attorney advertising' label)
Real estate: include brokerage name and license details where required; no claims about market direction presented as fact
Financial advisors: opinions are not advice; add the firm's required disclosure and avoid any return or income promise
